(i) in sodium-replete dogs AII causes renal vasoconstrictions and antidiuresis and (ii) in sodium-deplete dogs AII does not affect renal hemodynamics, glomerular filtration rate and diuresis.

in sodium replete animals AII produced renal vasodilatation, decreased GFR, and increased FF and that in sodium deplete animals, AII produced a less pronounced renal vasodilator response, with no change of GFR, but with an increase of FF and no change of diuresis.
In sodium-replete dogs, AII produced renal vasodilation, with increased GFR and FF, and antinatriuresi; the renal effects of AII were abolished by AIIA.

AII is a vasoconstrictor, but not a tubular antagonist in the kidney, and that the tubular response to AII is dependent on the sodium balance of the organism.
the renal effects of AII are dependent on sodium intake and the prevailing level of renal function.

The main takeaway from our work is that

in sodium replete animals AII produces renal vasoconstrictions and afferent arteriolar constriction with an increase in FF, which is accompanied by a decrease in GFR, diuresis, and natriuresis, but not kaliuresis; in sodium deplete animals the effects of AII on renal function are different and are mainly mediated by efferent arterioloar vasoconstriction.
